question.text: What will be the average price of diesel in the lower Atlantic U.S. on December 28, 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves as the average price of Lower Atlantic On-Highway Diesel in dollars per gallon for December 28, 2026 according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration's [Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update](https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/) for or closest to that date.

# Lower Atlantic on-highway diesel (EIA): research brief for the December 28, 2026 reading

The Lower Atlantic price was **$5.890/gal for the week of 2026-10-26**. That is about 46 cents below the U.S. average of $6.352. Nothing has happened yet that settles the question, and prices have been very volatile all year.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-27: EIA's Gasoline and Diesel Fuel Update was last released on October 27. The next release is November 3. [EIA](https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/)
- Data series: EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R1Z_DPG, Lower Atlantic (PADD 1C) On-Highway Diesel, weekly. Recent values: [EIA series](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R1Z_DPG&f=W)
  - Aug: 08/03 5.168, 08/10 5.034, 08/17 5.204, 08/24 5.350, 08/31 5.276
  - Sep: 09/07 5.605, 09/14 6.096, 09/21 **6.139** (2026 high), 09/28 5.953
  - Oct: 10/05 5.699, 10/12 5.645, 10/19 5.740, **10/26 5.890**
- The U.S. average for the same weeks: 09/21 6.529 (record), 10/05 6.199, 10/12 6.179, 10/19 6.276, 10/26 6.352. [EIA US series](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=EMD_EPD2D_PTE_NUS_DPG&f=W)
- The gap between the U.S. average and the Lower Atlantic has widened:
  - About $0.22-0.32 in August
  - $0.39 on 09/21
  - $0.50-0.54 for 10/05-10/19
  - $0.46 on 10/26
- The resolving figure will be the EIA reading for Monday, December 28, published about December 29.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The latest reading (5.890) sits in the middle of the question's range (4.4-6.8).
- Kalshi's weekly U.S. market for November 2 prices "above $6.26" at 0.97 and "above $6.30" at 0.24. That implies a U.S. average around $6.26-6.30 and a small drop from 6.352. The Lower Atlantic would probably edge down too, but I can't confirm that.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-01: Reuters, via Benzinga, reports that OPEC+ agreed in principle to keep December output targets unchanged. Brent has been rising. [Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/commodities/26/10/62765251/opec-plus-keeps-december-oil-output-targets-unchanged)
- 2026-10-30: Front-month NYMEX ULSD futures were about $4.79/gal. Distillate stocks were 102.8 million barrels, about 10% below the five-year average. This comes from a secondary dashboard search summary that I did not verify. [fueldataportal](https://fueldataportal.com/data/ulsd-diesel-futures)
- 2026-10-28/29: AAA put U.S. diesel at $6.35, up from $6.28 when the Trump-Putin diesel deal was announced. [Pravda.ua](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/10/29/8060230/index.amp)
- 2026-10-28: Experts say the Russian diesel deal benefits Moscow more than U.S. consumers. [Defense News](https://www.defensenews.com/global/europe/2026/10/28/trumps-russian-diesel-deal-benefits-moscow-more-than-us-consumers-experts-say/)
- 2026-10-13: The deal covers less than two weeks of U.S. demand. Goldman Sachs estimated it would cut wholesale prices by only $1-2 per barrel. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/13/trump-putin-zelenskyy-russia-ukraine-diesel-oil-price.html)
- 2026-10-09: Trump announced the deal: more than 300,000 tons immediately, 500,000 tons in November, then more. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/09/trump-putin-russian-diesel-us-global-markets.html)
- 2026-10-07/23: France is releasing 10 million barrels of diesel from strategic reserves. [fnp.de](https://www.fnp.de/verbraucher/diesel-frankreich-oelkonzern-senkt-preise-tanken-tankstellen-zr-94568329.html)
- Background drivers:
  - The Iran conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruptions, with markets reacting to peace-talk headlines. [FreightWaves](https://www.freightwaves.com/news/benchmark-price-is-up-futures-down-diesel-on-its-own)
  - Lost Middle East refining capacity and Russian refinery outages (2026-07-28 report, same FreightWaves source).
  - ULSD futures hit a record $5.262 on 2026-09-15.

## 4. Base rates and volatility
- In 2025 the Lower Atlantic fell from 3.642 (10/27) to 3.522 (12/29), a drop of 0.12. That was in a calm market.
- 2026 has been extremely volatile. Comparable 9-week moves in the Lower Atlantic series:
  - 03/02 → 05/04: +1.52 (Hormuz shock: 3.808 → 4.880 in a single week)
  - 04/06 → 06/08: −0.68
  - 07/06 → 09/07: +1.13
  - 09/21 → 10/26: −0.25
- Weekly moves of 0.1-0.5 have been common since March. The 2026 range so far is 3.484 to 6.139.
- Seasonal pattern: in normal years, retail diesel tends to drift lower from November into late December. 2026 has not followed normal patterns.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi markets on the **U.S. average**, not the Lower Atlantic. If the current ~$0.46 gap holds, subtract roughly that much.
  - Year-end (Dec 31): above $5.40 at 0.80, above $5.80 at 0.71, above $6.00 at 0.61, above $6.20 at 0.49, above $6.40 at 0.36, above $6.60 at 0.26, above $6.80 at 0.20, above $7.20 at 0.15. That puts the implied U.S. median near $6.20, and the tails are wide.
  - November 30: the U.S. median is near $6.40 (above $6.40 at 0.49).
  - 2026 high: above $6.60 at 0.66. Note the EIA U.S. weekly peak so far is already 6.529, so this market may be priced off a different source.
- Polymarket gives a U.S. diesel export ban by December 31 a 0.18 probability.
- EIA's October STEO (released 2026-10-06) forecast Q4 2026 U.S. retail diesel at $5.55 and Q4 Brent at $105. That diesel figure comes from a [Farm Progress](https://www.farmprogress.com/farm-policy/u-s-sees-diesel-stocks-falling-to-2003-low-ahead-of-peak-demand) report and is unverified. Actual prices are running well above it. [STEO Oct PDF](https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/archives/oct26.pdf)
- I found no forecast specific to the Lower Atlantic.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-11-01: OPEC+ meeting on December targets.
- 2026-11-03: U.S. Election Day and the EIA weekly release. EIA releases continue every Monday/Tuesday through December 29.
- 2026-11-10: November STEO.
- Early December: the December STEO and the next OPEC+ meeting.
- Russian diesel deliveries are scheduled for November, though there are doubts about whether Russia can export the promised volumes.
- Iran and Strait of Hormuz developments: peace-talk headlines have moved futures sharply.
- Winter heating-oil demand on the East Coast competes with diesel for the same distillate supply, and distillate stocks are already low.
- A possible U.S. diesel export ban (Polymarket 18%) and further administration pressure on refiners, per the Yahoo background article.

# Lower Atlantic On-Highway Diesel Price, December 28, 2026: Research Brief

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-10-27 release: the EIA series for Lower Atlantic (PADD 1C) on-highway diesel (EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R1Z_DPG) shows **$5.890 for the week of 10/26/2026**. The next release is 11/3/2026. [EIA series](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R1Z_DPG&f=W)
- Recent weekly Lower Atlantic values: 9/07 5.605; 9/14 6.096; **9/21 6.139 (2026 high)**; 9/28 5.953; 10/05 5.699; 10/12 5.645; 10/19 5.740; 10/26 5.890. [EIA](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R1Z_DPG&f=W)
- U.S. average on the same EIA basis: 9/21 6.529; 10/05 6.199; 10/12 6.179; 10/19 6.276; 10/26 6.352. [EIA U.S. series](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=EMD_EPD2D_PTE_NUS_DPG&f=W)
- **The Lower Atlantic price has run well below the U.S. average:** −0.46 on 10/26, −0.54 on 10/19, −0.53 on 10/12, −0.50 on 10/05, −0.39 on 9/21. In late July the gap was only about −0.06 (5.255 vs 5.313). This matters if you convert national market prices into a regional estimate.
- December 28 is a Monday, so it should be a normal EIA survey date, although the holiday week could delay the release.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. The latest value ($5.89) sits in the lower-middle of the 4.4 to 6.8 question range, and there are about 8.5 weeks of price movement left.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-01: OPEC+ reportedly agreed in principle to keep December output targets unchanged; Brent is rising. [Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/commodities/26/10/62765251/opec-plus-keeps-december-oil-output-targets-unchanged)
- 2026-10-31: CNBC puts diesel at $6.32/gal. Brent rose more than 13% in October. Markets are pricing in the risk of renewed fighting with Iran after the Nov 3 vote (Trump has said there will be no strikes before the midterms). The Russia deal covers about 6M barrels through November, which analysts call immaterial. A U.S. export ban was considered and rejected. [CNBC](https://cnbc.com/2026/10/31/trump-gas-diesel-price-midterm-election.html)
- 2026-10-30: per WSJ/AAA, the national diesel average reached $6.35 on Oct 28 and rose about 7 cents after the Trump-Putin diesel announcement. [capital.ua](https://www.capital.ua/ru/news/180676-wsj-ugoda-iz-rosiyeyu-ne-dopomozhe-suttyevo-zniziti-tsini-na-palne-u-ssha-ta-sviti)
- 2026-10-31: Russia's ban on diesel exports by producers was due to expire. I could not confirm whether it was extended. The ban on non-producers runs to 1/31/2027, and the Kremlin partly lifted the ban to carry out the U.S. deal. [Interfax](https://interfax.com/newsroom/top-stories/119335/), [CNBC 10/27](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/27/trump-putin-zelenskyy-russia-ukraine-diesel.html)
- 2026-10-27: the diesel crack spread was reported at about $85/bbl over Brent. [search summary of Macrotrends/others](https://www.macrotrends.net/3401/us-diesel-prices)
- 2026-10-13: U.S. diesel futures jumped about 5%. Brent was about $106. [NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/business/energy/diesel-futures-higher-prices-trump-moves-rcna603218)
- 2026-10-05: Trump's executive order allows red-dyed (tax-exempt) diesel on highways, with the federal tax deferred through year-end. [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/05/business/trump-diesel-prices-executive-order), [White House](https://www.whitehouse.gov/releases/2026/10/president-trump-takes-decisive-action-to-lower-diesel-costs-for-american-truckers-farmers/)
- 2026-10-06: EIA's October STEO forecasts Brent at $105 for Q4 2026 and U.S. diesel above $6 in October, then declining gradually to about $4.50 average in 2027. East Coast distillate stocks were 32% below the 5-year average in September and are expected to stay 20-30% below through winter. [EIA STEO](https://www.eia.gov/outlooks/steo/pdf/steo_full.pdf), [press release](https://www.eia.gov/pressroom/releases/press593.php)

## 4. Base rates and variation
- Same window last year: Lower Atlantic went from 3.642 (10/27/2025) to 3.522 (12/29/2025), down 0.12. That fits the usual seasonal drift into late December. [EIA](https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R1Z_DPG&f=W)
- Volatility in 2026 is far above normal. Over spans of about 8-9 weeks:
  - 3/02 to 4/06: up 1.82 (war shock)
  - 4/06 to 6/29: down 1.08
  - 7/06 to 9/14: up 1.62
  - 9/21 to 10/12: down 0.49 in 3 weeks
- In 2026, typical changes of ±0.5 to 1.0 over 8 weeks have been common. Calmer years usually see ±0.1 to 0.3.
- 2026 range for the Lower Atlantic: low 4.477 (7/06), high 6.139 (9/21).

## 5. Other forecasts
These Kalshi markets are on the **U.S. national** price, probably the AAA basis, not the Lower Atlantic.
- Year-end (12/31) market: about 49% above $6.20, 61% above $6.00, 71% above $5.80, 36% above $6.40, 20% above $6.80. That puts the implied median near $6.20.
- November 30 market: implied median about $6.40.
- Nov 2 week market: 97% above $6.26 and 24% above $6.30.
- Converting to the Lower Atlantic with the recent EIA gap of about −0.45 to −0.50 suggests a regional median around $5.70-5.75. This conversion is my arithmetic, not a market price, and the gap itself has moved between about −0.06 and −0.54 this year.
- Polymarket: 18% chance of a U.S. diesel export ban announced by Dec 31.
- EIA STEO (Oct): gradual decline from above $6 national, with no regional figure.
- I found no forecast specific to the Lower Atlantic.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 11/3: U.S. midterms. CNBC reports markets see a risk that Iran hostilities resume afterward.
- 11/3: next weekly EIA release; weekly releases continue through 12/28 (released about 12/29).
- About 11/10: EIA's November STEO; about 12/9: December STEO.
- Late November / December: whether Russia extends its producer export ban, and how many diesel barrels the U.S.-Russia deal actually delivers.
- Ongoing: Strait of Hormuz transits (about 32/day in early October vs 130-140 before the war) and Houthi or Ukrainian strikes on refineries. [Admiral Markets](https://admiralmarkets.com/analytics/traders-blog/diesel-shortage-october-2026)
- Winter heating demand while East Coast distillate stocks stay low.
- Year-end expiry of the red-dyed diesel tax deferral.
- OPEC+ decisions after December.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) **Time left:** about 8 weeks. The resolving reading is EIA's December 28, 2026 value, published around December 29.

(b) **Latest value:** $5.890/gal for the Lower Atlantic, week of October 26, 2026. The U.S. average that week was $6.352.

(c) **If nothing changed:** about $5.89.

(d) **If the trend continued:** the October trend is mildly up, rising from 5.645 to 5.890 over three weeks. Kalshi's weekly market points to a small dip on November 2, so the short-term trend is unclear. Extending the October rise would give roughly $6.1-6.3. Normal seasonality, where diesel drifts lower in December, would give about $5.6-5.7.

(e) **Historical variation:** in 2026, 9-week moves in this series have ranged from about -0.7 to +1.5. Weekly swings of $0.10-0.50 have been common. Calm years move only about ±$0.15 over the same stretch.

(f) **Experts and markets:**
- Kalshi's year-end U.S. average market has a median near $6.20 with wide tails: 80% above $5.40 and 20% above $6.80.
- The gap between the U.S. average and the Lower Atlantic has been $0.39-0.54 recently. Subtracting about $0.42 implies a Lower Atlantic median near $5.75-5.80.
- EIA's October STEO put Q4 U.S. diesel at $5.55, which is below the current price.
- Low distillate stocks and winter heating-oil demand support prices.
- The Russian diesel deal and a possible U.S. export ban are modest downside factors.

(g) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** an Iran peace deal reopens Hormuz flows fully, and an export ban plus Russian cargoes collapse distillate cracks. The Lower Atlantic could fall to around $4.5-4.8.
- **High:** Hormuz is disrupted again or Russian refinery outages escalate, during a cold East Coast winter with distillate stocks at 2003 lows. The Lower Atlantic could rise above $6.8-7.2.

**How I set the distribution:** I took the Kalshi-implied U.S. distribution, shifted it down by the regional gap, and narrowed the extreme tails slightly, because the thin markets look overly wide.
